The Earthquakes initially took the lead, but Bryan Ramírez quickly brought Cincinnati level. San Jose then regained their advantage, holding it for much of the second half. The turning point arrived in the final ten minutes, as Tom Barlow equalized in the 80th minute, setting the stage for a dramatic finish.

Just two minutes after Barlow's goal, Evander netted the go-ahead strike, sending the home crowd into a frenzy. Ayoub Jabbari then put the result beyond doubt in stoppage time, completing a thrilling turnaround for FC Cincinnati and securing all three points in a match that will be remembered for its late drama.

articles.headline: CAF Hails Oshoala as Super Falcons Edge Zambia in WAFCON Thriller
articles.summary: The Confederation of African Football has lauded Nigerian striker Asisat Oshoala following her decisive performance, scoring the lone goal in the Super Falcons' narrow 1-0 victory over Zambia in the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations. Oshoala's early strike proved crucial, securing three vital points for Nigeria despite finishing the match with ten players.
articles.body:
Asisat Oshoala proved her enduring class in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations, delivering the match-winning goal for Nigeria against Zambia in a tense Group C encounter. Reinstated to the starting lineup after being a substitute in their previous surprising loss to Malawi, Oshoala wasted no time, finding the net just eight minutes into the game.

The prolific forward demonstrated her predatory instincts, latching onto a precise long pass from captain Rasheedat Ajibade. Oshoala outmaneuvered a Zambian defender with her pace before calmly slotting the ball past the opposing goalkeeper, giving the Super Falcons an early and critical advantage.

Despite playing a significant portion of the match with only ten players after Tosin Demehin received a red card for a challenge on Barbra Banda, Nigeria held firm to secure the victory. CAF's recognition highlights Oshoala's influential role and tireless effort, which ultimately propelled her team to a crucial win.

articles.headline: Sanabria Earns Uruguay Call-Up for Crucial World Cup Qualifiers
articles.summary: Uruguayan forward Sanabria has received a national team call-up, set to join his compatriots for upcoming FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifying matches. The selection highlights his recent club form, positioning him for potential involvement in vital international fixtures.
articles.body:
The Uruguayan national team has brought LA Galaxy striker Sanabria into the fold for their highly anticipated 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign. The forward is expected to link up with the squad ahead of two significant matches in October.

Sanabria's inclusion comes as Uruguay prepares to face Peru on October 11, followed by a clash against Ecuador on October 15. These fixtures are crucial as nations vie for qualification spots in the expanded World Cup tournament.

Before his move to the LA Galaxy, Sanabria showcased his scoring prowess with Club Nacional, netting five goals and contributing four assists across 46 appearances. His consistent performance has clearly caught the eye of the national team selectors, offering a fresh attacking option for the upcoming challenges.

articles.headline: Real Madrid Squander Two-Goal Advantage in Fiorentina Pre-Season Draw
articles.summary: Real Madrid let a comfortable lead slip away, settling for a 2-2 draw against Fiorentina in their latest pre-season friendly. Despite an early offensive surge, Jose Mourinho's side was unable to maintain their advantage against the Italian visitors.
articles.body:
Real Madrid's pre-season preparations hit a minor snag as they played out a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina on August 1st. The Spanish giants initially looked strong, with young sensation Endrick opening the scoring in the 12th minute, followed by Alex Ciria extending their lead just twelve minutes later.

However, the second half saw a shift in momentum, as the Serie A side mounted a comeback. Roberto Piccoli pulled one back for Fiorentina, before Mois Keane found the equalizer, ensuring the spoils were shared.

Manager Jose Mourinho utilized the friendly to assess his squad, handing a start to recent acquisition Denzel Dumfries. Despite the disappointing result, the match provided valuable minutes for several players as the team continues to build towards the upcoming La Liga season.

articles.headline: Inter Milan Secures World Cup Winner Romero from Tottenham in €40 Million Deal
articles.summary: Inter Milan has reportedly finalized an agreement with Tottenham Hotspur for the transfer of defender Cristian Romero, a move set to bolster the Italian club's Champions League aspirations. The Argentine World Cup winner's departure marks a significant shift in Tottenham's defensive lineup as new manager Roberto De Zerbi begins to reshape the squad.
articles.body:
Inter Milan has successfully reached an agreement with Tottenham Hotspur to acquire the services of highly-rated central defender Cristian Romero. Reports indicate that the Serie A giants will pay approximately €40 million (£34.5 million) for the Argentine international, with talks accelerating over the past few days. This transfer will see Romero join a club competing in the Champions League, a prospect that likely appealed to the accomplished defender.

The move comes as Tottenham's new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, navigates his initial transfer window in North London. While losing a player of Romero's caliber might seem a blow, the timing could be beneficial for Spurs, who have already secured two proven defenders this summer. This suggests the club is prepared for such a high-profile departure, aiming to balance their books after significant midfield acquisitions.

Romero's exit allows him to pursue Champions League football with Inter, while Tottenham continues its squad overhaul. The transfer fee received will provide De Zerbi with further resources to fine-tune his team ahead of the new season, indicating a strategic approach to player movements at the club.

articles.headline: Danso's Rapid Red Card and Chelsea's Defensive Woes Mar Sydney Friendly
articles.summary: Tottenham's pre-season clash with Chelsea in Sydney saw a swift red card for Kevin Danso, just minutes after his introduction. The match, which Spurs won 2-1, also highlighted ongoing defensive vulnerabilities for Chelsea, prompting early season scrutiny.
articles.body:
The pre-season friendly between Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in Sydney produced a moment of significant drama when Spurs defender Kevin Danso received a red card merely three minutes after entering the game. Introduced at halftime, Danso was dismissed in the 48th minute for bringing down Chelsea forward Joao Pedro, who was clear on goal. Despite the exhibition nature of the contest, the referee promptly issued the red card, leaving Tottenham to play with ten men for the majority of the second half.

Tottenham ultimately secured a 2-1 victory in the encounter, with Estevao's equalizer for Chelsea canceling out Sandro Tonali's initial goal for Spurs, before a late winner for Tottenham. However, beyond the scoreline and Danso's early exit, the match brought renewed attention to Chelsea's defensive struggles. Analysts noted the team's backline appeared vulnerable, a continuation of concerns from the previous season.

Head coach Xabi Alonso now faces the task of addressing these defensive weaknesses as the new Premier League season approaches. While pre-season friendlies often serve as opportunities for experimentation and fitness building, the recurring defensive issues against a rival like Tottenham will undoubtedly be a focal point for the Blues as they prepare for the competitive campaign. Reinforcements have been made, but their impact on overall solidity remains to be seen.

articles.headline: Méndez Debut Equalizer Halts Miami's Streak After Suárez Stunner
articles.summary: Columbus Crew newcomer Brais Méndez delivered a dramatic late equalizer in his Major League Soccer debut, securing a 2-2 draw against Inter Miami on Saturday. This result snapped Miami's impressive six-game winning streak, despite a spectacular long-range goal from Luis Suárez earlier in the match.
articles.body:
Inter Miami's formidable winning run was brought to an end as the Columbus Crew earned a hard-fought 2-2 draw at Nu Stadium. The match saw Uruguayan star Luis Suárez open the scoring in the 16th minute with a breathtaking strike from distance, adding to his impressive goal tally for the season. However, the home side's lead was nullified by an own goal from Casemiro in the 34th minute, setting the stage for a back-and-forth contest.

Noah Allen restored Miami's advantage with a header just before halftime, giving them a 2-1 lead. The highly anticipated return of Lionel Messi from World Cup duty saw him enter the game as a substitute in the 53rd minute, though he couldn't find the decisive goal to secure a victory.

The drama peaked in the 84th minute when Columbus Crew's new signing, Brais Méndez, marked his MLS debut with a crucial equalizer. His curling free-kick found the back of the net, denying Miami three points and ending their club-record winning streak, although their unbeaten run now extends to seven matches.
